correctness.rationale: The proof uses the published irrotational single-well/unique-resonance lemma as a named premise and independently derives each new conclusion. The sequence y_n=n x_n is strictly increasing and bounded by the sole upper-branch crossing y_B; its limit follows from phase-speed continuity. A nonzero increasing-branch derivative yields the cubic n^{-3} coefficient with O(n^{-5}) remainder. A positive Taylor-series inequality at B=1/3 and a divided-difference estimate establish the all-n O(delta) bound. The global B-to-zero supremum follows from a sequential contradiction: alpha=nB tends to 0, a finite positive value or infinity; exact residuals have sign limits 1-c^2, tanh(c)-alpha*c^2 and c-c^2 respectively. The X profile is unique. The standalone stdlib script completed VERIFICATION_OK 329; finite samples are supplementary, not proofs.

value.rationale: The same family of Wilton resonances exhibits two noncommuting small-tension and high-harmonic limits. The universally normalized alpha=nB crossover classifies all integer orders at once and connects the deep-water root x~(nB)^(-1/2) to the finite-depth long-wave root x~(nB)^(-1). The all-order 45 delta critical scaling gives a sharp leading coefficient while n varies, and the fixed-B cubic correction resolves limiting short-wave placement. This is a physically motivated complete parameter-crossover law, not a renamed isolated evaluation. It makes no unsupported claim of nonlinear or experimental significance.
